classification.difficultyReason: Choose a conjugate, apply the difference of squares and expand surd numerators.

content.prompt: Express each number with a rational denominator.

answer.worked:
Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{5}-2$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=\frac{3\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{5}-2)}{(\sqrt{5}+2)(\sqrt{5}-2)}\\\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=\frac{3\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt{2}}{5-4}\\\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=3\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt{2}\end{align*}$$

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2\sqrt{3}+1$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}-1}&=\frac{\sqrt{3}(2\sqrt{3}+1)}{(2\sqrt{3}-1)(2\sqrt{3}+1)}\\\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}-1}&=\frac{6+\sqrt{3}}{12-1}\\\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}-1}&=\frac{6+\sqrt{3}}{11}\end{align*}$$

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{5}-2$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{3\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=\frac{(3\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{5}-2)}{(\sqrt{5}+2)(\sqrt{5}-2)}\\\frac{3\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=\frac{3\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{5}-2}{5-4}\\\frac{3\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{5}+2}&=3\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{5}-6\sqrt{2}-2\end{align*}$$

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}}&=\frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})}{(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})}\\\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}}&=\frac{\sqrt{6}-2+\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{3-2}\\\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}}&=\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{3}-2-\sqrt{2}\end{align*}$$
